study type: secondary analysis of a multicenter randomized controlled trial
outcome: rotation from OP to OA position during the first stage of labor
cohort: 285 laboring women with ruptured membranes and a term fetus in occiput posterior position were included.
finding: Rotation of the fetal head from occiput posterior to occiput anterior was negatively associated with excessive gestational weight gain, macrosomia, direct OP position, and prelabor rupture of membranes, while oxytocin administration was positively associated with fetal head rotation.
mod_finding: Oxytocin administration was the only factor positively associated with fetal head rotation, an outcome that facilitates vaginal birth.
